scope: plain-language draft and the claims it cites

overall.summary: All 214 claims and every number in the draft reproduce, but several part-only numbers are written as the model's predicted chance; for state government this reverses the direction (the model raises the typical person's chance from 72% to 78%; the draft says it barely lowers it to 71%). Smaller issues: the Yugoslavia, Trinidad and preschool part-only figures, the 26 Thailand-born described as an early onset, the age minimum (46 not 47), the hours knee (50 not 49) and the size of the sex effect.

findings.statement: while working for a state government moves it [the predicted chance of a low income] from about 72% to about 71%
findings.check: probe --claim C182 (typical person, private -> state government), whole model
findings.evidence: C182 is a part-scope number (this part's contribution changes by -0.005). In the model the typical person's predicted chance goes from 71.5% (private) to 78.4% (state government): it rises by about 7 points, not falls by 1. The sentence names the predicted chance, so its direction is wrong for the model; it holds only for this part's contribution. The same reading is in readdown.ann_117.hypothesis[0], readdown.ann_117.evidence[0] and the ann_117 hypothesis revision.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --claim C182
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --set workclass=7

findings.statement: Working for a state government barely moves it: from about 72% to about 71%.
findings.evidence: True of this part only (contribution -0.0048 vs 0); the model's prediction moves 71.5% -> 78.4% because the linear terms read work class too. Needs 'through this part'.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --set workclass=7

findings.statement: Being born in Yugoslavia rather than elsewhere lowers the predicted chance ... from about 72% to about 42%
findings.evidence: 42% is the part-only figure. The model's prediction for a typical Yugoslavia-born person is 51.2% (the linear terms move from -0.98 to -0.62 once the person is not US-born). Direction right, size overstated for the model. Same in annotations.ann_117[0], readdown.ann_117.evidence[0] and the revision.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --set native-country=41

findings.statement: Being born in Trinidad and Tobago rather than elsewhere raises the predicted chance ... from about 72% to about 94%
findings.evidence: 94% is the part-only figure; the model predicts 95.9% for the typical Trinidad-born person. Direction right, small scope gap. Same in annotations.ann_118[1] and readdown.ann_118.evidence[1].
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --set native-country=38

findings.statement: A preschool education ... raises the predicted chance for a typical person with that education (and the education level of 1 such people have in the data) from about 72% to about 91%
findings.evidence: The 91% case keeps the education level at 9 (this part does not read education level). A typical person with preschool and education level 1, as the sentence describes, gets 99.6% from the model. Direction right; the stated case and the number do not match. Same in annotations.ann_121[1] and readdown.ann_121.evidence[1].
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --claim C173

findings.statement: through it age adds to the predicted chance ... once it rises above about 46 years; for 26 of the 39073 training people it already acts below that
findings.check: subgroup native-country=='37'; subgroup age<=46.1; probe Thailand-born age sweep
findings.evidence: The 26 are the Thailand-born (no fold: the part acts on all 26 at every age). Only 21 of them are below 46 years, and below about 42 years the part lowers their predicted chance (contribution -2.63 at 17 years, -0.44 at 38 years) rather than adding to it. The sentence does not say who they are, and the 'adds' context misleads. Same in annotations.ann_124[1] and readdown.ann_124.evidence[2].
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --where "`native-country` == '37'"
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --where "age <= 46.1"
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --set native-country=37 --sweep age=17:74:12

findings.statement: the whole model's chance is lowest at about 47 years and higher either side
findings.evidence: Lowest at 46 to 46.5 years (56.1% at 46, 56.2% at 46.5, 56.6% at 47). The model is piecewise linear in log-odds, so the minimum sits at the age-hinge knee, 46.1 years, which the same draft calls 'about 46'. About a year off; the claim's grid point (46.9) is coarse. Same in annotations.ann_129[6], readdown.ann_124.hypothesis[0], readdown.ann_129.hypothesis[0], worth_checking[3] and the ann_124 revision.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --sweep age=45:48:7
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --sweep age=22:82:31

findings.statement: the chance is lowest at about 47 years and higher either side, so it rises again after middle age: from about 89% at 22 years to about 65% at 58 years
findings.evidence: The rise is real (56.1% at 46 -> 64.6% at 58 -> 78.2% at 80), but the two numbers quoted (89% -> 65%) show a fall and do not evidence the rise being flagged.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-19b0f0 --hold typical --sweep age=22:82:31

findings.statement: Working more hours lowers it steadily up to about 49 hours, then no further
findings.evidence: The hours part contributes +0.2517 at 45 h and 0 at 50 h, slope 0.051 per hour, so it ends at 49.9 hours: about 50, as the hours block itself says. '49' is outside rounding and inconsistent with the hours block. Same in readdown.ann_129.hypothesis[0].

findings.statement: marriage and sex move the predicted chance ... by large amounts
findings.evidence: Changing sex alone moves the typical person from 71.5% to 80.6%. The 72% -> 99% of C010 comes from the linked change to never married and not in a family. Marriage moves it a lot; sex alone moderately.
